nodes.title: ABOUT
widgets_values:
# 25 fps Delivery: Native, Conform or Retime

**Three ways to hand over 25 fps video from ComfyUI.** Which one you use depends on a single question: does the model let you choose the frame rate?

| | Route | Use it when | What it costs you |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Native 25** (LTX 2.5) | the model takes a frame rate | nothing, every frame is generated at 25 |
| **B** | **Conform** (core nodes) | the clip is 24 fps and has no sync sound | plays 4% faster (5.0 s becomes 4.8 s) |
| **C** | **Retime** (partner node) | the clip is 24 fps and length or sound must hold | new in-between frames are generated |

## How to use
1. In **group 1**, write a prompt and set the length. The delivery frame rate is already 25.
2. Press **Run**. Three files are saved to `output/25fps/`: `A_native`, `B_conform` and `C_retime`.
3. To convert MiniMax H3 instead of Seedance, turn on the **★ switch** in group 1.

**Orange nodes** are every place a frame rate is set. **Green nodes** are your inputs.

## Which model does what
- **LTX 2.5** takes the frame rate as an input. Open weights (Route A here) and the LTX partner node both offer 25.
- **MiniMax H3** open weights are trained at 24 fps and have no frame-rate input, so H3 is a 24 fps source.
- **Seedance 2.5** (and most closed models) return 24 fps with no option to change it.

## Do I need a custom node?
No. Route B is two core nodes. Route C is one partner node after the generator. Core frame interpolation only makes whole multiples (x2, x3...), and 24 to 25 is not a whole multiple, so the partner node does the retime.

## Running only one route
Each route ends in its own Save Video. To skip a route, select its group and mute it (Ctrl+M).
Route A runs on open weights and needs the LTX 2.5 files in group 2. Routes B and C need no local models unless the H3 switch is on.

nodes.title: NOTE | Inputs
widgets_values: **NOTE | Inputs.** One prompt and one length feed every route, so the three results are comparable. The delivery frame rate drives every orange node in Routes A and B.

nodes.title: ★ Prompt
widgets_values: A red tram glides through a rainy European city street at dusk. Wet cobblestones reflect the shop lights, people with umbrellas cross in front of the camera, and the camera tracks slowly sideways with the tram. Natural light, shallow depth of field, 35mm film look. Sound of rain, footsteps and a tram bell.

inputs.name: value
inputs.label: Convert MiniMax H3 instead of Seedance

nodes.title: ★ Convert MiniMax H3 instead of Seedance
NOTE | LTX 2.5 models
widgets_values: **NOTE | LTX 2.5 models.** Already on Comfy Cloud. Running locally, the files go in `diffusion_models`, `text_encoders` and `vae`. The bf16 files also work if you have the memory for them.

nodes.title: NOTE | Native 25 fps
widgets_values: **NOTE | Native 25 fps.** LTX is told the frame rate while it generates, so motion and sound are made for 25 fps and nothing is converted afterwards. The frame rate goes in **three places** (the orange nodes): the conditioning, the audio latent and the saved file. All three read the value from group 1. LTX frame counts are 8n+1, so 5 s at 25 fps is 121 frames (4.84 s).

nodes.title: Negative prompt (never leave empty)
widgets_values: worst quality, inconsistent motion, blurry, jittery, distorted, warped faces, flickering

nodes.title: Frame count = seconds x fps (LTX needs 8n+1)
Frame rate, 3 of 3: the saved file
NOTE | Seedance 2.5
widgets_values: **NOTE | Seedance 2.5.** A closed model. The node has no frame-rate input and the clip always comes back at 24 fps, so it is converted afterwards (Routes B and C). Any other 24 fps generator works the same way: swap this node for Kling, Veo or a Load Video node.

nodes.title: NOTE | MiniMax H3
widgets_values: **NOTE | MiniMax H3.** H3 is trained at 24 fps and has no frame-rate input, so open weights do not make it a native 25 fps model. It joins the same conversion as Seedance. H3 frame counts sit on a 17n+5 grid counted at 24 fps (5 s = 124 frames). This group is skipped unless the switch in group 1 is on.

nodes.title: H3 clip at its own 24 fps
NOTE | The 24 fps clip
widgets_values: **NOTE | The 24 fps clip.** The switch passes on one clip, and only that generator runs. The readout shows the frame rate the model delivered, which is the problem this workflow solves: expect 24.

nodes.title: NOTE | Conform
widgets_values: **NOTE | Conform.** The same frames are written at 25 fps instead of 24. Nothing is generated, so every frame is exactly what the model made. The clip plays 4% faster (5.0 s becomes 4.8 s), the classic film-to-PAL conversion. **Picture only:** the sound would drift out of sync, so it is left off. For clips with dialogue or music, use Route C.

nodes.title: Write the same frames at 25 fps
RESULT B · Conformed to 25 fps (picture only)
NOTE | Retime
widgets_values: **NOTE | Retime.** One partner node after the generator. Topaz frame interpolation builds a true 25 fps clip of the same length, so sound stays in sync. The upscaler is switched off, so the picture is only retimed and the look does not change. Set the same frame rate here as in group 1 (this input is a whole number). The readout proves the result: expect 25.

nodes.title: NOTE | vCube alternative
widgets_values: **NOTE | vCube alternative.** Same job from Seedance's own vendor: set `fps` to 25 and it interpolates to a true 25 fps. It also cleans up and sharpens the picture, so use it when you want an enhance or upscale pass in the same step. Both nodes are muted so a run is not billed twice. Select them and press Ctrl+M to use this instead of group 8.

nodes.title: RESULT C (alt) · Retimed to 25 fps by vCube
